title: Symmetric cubical lines extend over a normal semiabelian base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Here a commutative group scheme has addition, inverse and identity $e$ satisfying the commutative group identities, and separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Suppose every geometric fibre is semiabelian: over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$, it is an extension, exact as fppf sheaves, $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_k\to A_k\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication, and $A_k$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Restriction from cubical rigidified lines on $G$ to cubical rigidified lines on $G_U$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line] is fully faithful: for any two such lines on $G$, each cubical rigidification-preserving isomorphism between their restrictions extends uniquely to such an isomorphism on $G$. Moreover, if $(N,r,\tau)$ is a cubical rigidified line on $G_U$ and its underlying invertible module is symmetric, meaning $[-1]^*N\simeq N$ with tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback], then it extends to a cubical rigidified line $(B,r_B,\tau_B)$ on $G$, with a cubical rigidification-preserving isomorphism $B|_{G_U}\simeq N$. No positivity hypothesis on $N$ is imposed, and no ampleness conclusion on $B$ is asserted.

source.place: II 3.2.1--3.2.3 (full faithfulness) and II 3.3 (symmetric essential image). Local original WANTED. Online cross-check: Lan, revised thesis, Proposition 3.3.2.2(1) and Theorem 3.3.2.3(2), printed p.70.

proof.text: First prove full faithfulness for rigidified lines. For two lines $L,M$ on $G$ and a rigidification-preserving isomorphism $a_U:L_U\simeq M_U$, view $a_U$ as a nonzero rational section of $M\otimes L^{-1}$. By [lem-sfb-normal-group-vertical-cartier-descent], $G$ is normal integral, $G_U$ is dense, and its divisor $D$ satisfies $D=p^*e^*D$. Along $e_U$ the section is the isomorphism determined by the two given rigidifications. This extends along $e$ as that same isomorphism, so $e^*D=0$. Thus $D=0$ and the rational section is an everywhere invertible regular section. It gives an extension $a:L\simeq M$ preserving rigidifications; uniqueness follows because the rational section is determined on the dense open. By [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b), every such isomorphism preserves the given cube sections. This proves the first clause. The argument applies after replacing $S$ by any nonempty open of it.

source.place: II 3.2.1--3.2.3; I 2.6 for preservation of cube sections.

proof.text: For existence, apply [lem-sfb-rigidified-line-big-open-extension] to $(N,r)$, obtaining $V\supseteq U$ and $(N_V,r_V)$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}\geq2$ outside $V$. Give $N_V$ its unique cube section by [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b); its identification over $U$ respects cube sections by the same node. Normalize the given underlying symmetry by multiplying it by the inverse of its value along $e_U$, so that it preserves $r$. It is then cubical by that node. Apply step 1 over $V$ to extend this isomorphism to $[-1]^*N_V\simeq N_V$, preserving rigidification and cube. Normality, smoothness, finite presentation and semiabelian geometric fibres persist on these open restrictions.

source.place: II 3.2.2--3.2.3 and II 3.3.3, reduction to a complement of codimension at least two.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-symmetric-line-power-prolongation] and work on one nonempty member $W$ of its affine base covering. Replace $S,U,V,G$ by their restrictions to $W$ for steps 3--7. We have $d\geq1$, a line $P$ on $G$, and an isomorphism $P_U\simeq N^{\otimes d}$. Put $Q=P^{\otimes d}\otimes p^*(e^*P)^{\otimes(-d)}$. Tensor inverse, tensor product and pullback of lines are lines by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. The cancellation at $e$ canonically rigidifies $Q$, and the given isomorphism and $r$ identify $Q_U$ with $N^{\otimes d^2}$ as rigidified lines. Give $Q$ its unique cube section by [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b). By [lem-sfb-cubical-symmetric-multiplication-square], $[d]^*N_V\simeq N_V^{\otimes d^2}$ as cubical rigidified lines. Step 1 over $V$ extends the given isomorphism on $U$ to an isomorphism $b:Q|_{G_V}\simeq[d]^*N_V$. It preserves rigidifications and cube sections.

source.place: II 3.3.3, power prolongation and the I 5.5 multiplication formula.

proof.text: Put $q=[d]:G\to G$. By [lem-sfb-semiabelian-multiplication-fppf], $q$ is an fpqc cover and its double and triple relation schemes $R_2,R_3$ are flat, of finite presentation over $S$ and locally Noetherian. On $R_2|_V$, use $b$ and the equality $q\operatorname{pr}_1=q\operatorname{pr}_2$ to define $\alpha_V:\operatorname{pr}_1^*Q\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*Q$: explicitly $\alpha_V=(\operatorname{pr}_2^*b)^{-1}\operatorname{pr}_1^*b$, with the two pullbacks of $N_V$ canonically identified. Cancellation gives $\alpha_{23,V}\alpha_{12,V}=\alpha_{13,V}$ on $R_3|_V$. We use the flat relation schemes themselves; their kernels need not be reduced, and the multiplication map need not be finite.

source.place: II 3.3.3, descent along multiplication; explicit descent isomorphism.

proof.text: At a point $y$ of $R_2$ or $R_3$ lying above $s\in S\setminus V$, the local ring map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{R_a,y}$ is flat between Noetherian local rings by step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] and the definition [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{S,s}\geq2$. The formula [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] gives $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{R_a,y}\geq2$. Any line at $y$ is a free module of rank one and has this same depth. Thus [lem-sbc-depth-two-hartogs-restriction] applies to every Hom line between the indicated pullbacks of $Q$ on $R_2$ and $R_3$. In particular their sections restrict bijectively to the corresponding restrictions over $V$. This is a direct application of the three depth statements, with no regularity, reducedness or invertibility-of-$d$ assumption on the relation schemes.

source.place: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal) and Tag 0337 (lemma-apply-grothendieck); divisors.tex Tag 0E9I (lemma-depth-2-hartog).

proof.text: Use the section bijections of step 5 on $R_2$ to extend both $\alpha_V$ and its inverse. Their composites equal the identity because this is true over $V$ and restriction is injective for the endomorphism lines. The extension is therefore an isomorphism $\alpha:\operatorname{pr}_1^*Q\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*Q$. On $R_3$, the two sections $\alpha_{23}\alpha_{12}$ and $\alpha_{13}$ agree over $V$, so the same injectivity proves their equality globally. Consequently $(Q,\alpha)$ is an fpqc descent datum for $q$.

source.place: II 3.3.3; extension of the descent datum by the Hartogs bijections established in step 5.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](1),(3), this datum descends to an invertible module $B$ on the target $G$, with a compatible identification $c:q^*B\simeq Q$. Over $V$, the map $b\circ c$ is compatible with the canonical descent data on $q_V^*B_V$ and $q_V^*N_V$. The full faithfulness in that same node descends it to an isomorphism $B|_{G_V}\simeq N_V$. Since $q\circ e=e$, pulling $c$ back along the identity and using the rigidification of $Q$ gives $r_B:e^*B\simeq\mathcal O_S$; the isomorphism over $V$ respects it because $b$ does. Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b) to $(B,r_B)$. Its unique cube structure makes the isomorphism over $V$, and hence the prescribed one over $U$, cubical. This finishes the construction on $W$.

source.place: II 3.3.3, effective descent; Stacks Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent); I 2.6.

proof.text: Restore the covering $S=\bigcup W_i$. Over $W_i\cap W_j$, the two constructed cubical rigidified lines have the specified identification over the dense open $U\cap W_i\cap W_j$. Step 1 extends it uniquely. On triple overlaps these identifications satisfy the cocycle condition because they do so over $U$ and extension is unique. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descent](3) to this Zariski covering of $G$ and its compatible line-module isomorphisms, obtaining a global line $B$. Full faithfulness for module maps in the same node glues its rigidifications; [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](b) supplies the unique global cube structure and makes its identification with $N$ over $U$ cubical. Thus $B$ is the required extension. Every construction used symmetry but no positivity of $N$, so it yields exactly the stated existence conclusion.

source.place: II 3.3, Zariski assembly after the local descent construction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q14-746b17b5f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all five new nodes in full. Moret-Bailly is not in literature/ (WANTED, proof_origin agent is correct), so I checked the item against Lan's revised thesis, printed p.194: Prop 3.3.2.2(1), full faithfulness over a normal base, and Thm 3.3.2.3(2), symmetric underlying torsor lies in the essential image with no ampleness and no requirement that G_U be abelian. The 8 steps are MB II 3.3.3's actual argument. 1: the vertical-Cartier divisor D=p*e*D, with e*D=0 from the rigidifications, gives full faithfulness; cubes come from semiabelian-cubical-rigidification(b). 2: big-open extension plus the symmetry normalized at e. 3: Q=P^d⊗p*(e*P)^{-d}, the [d]*N=N^{d²} formula, and step 1 over V give b. 4: α_V=(pr2*b)^{-1}pr1*b on the flat relation schemes. 5: S2 from Serre's criterion, the flat local depth formula, and the Hartogs depth-two node. 6: the datum and its inverse extend elementarily. 7: fpqc descent and its full faithfulness descend along [d], r_B comes from q∘e=e, and (b) gives the cube. 8: Zariski gluing through step-1 uniqueness. I checked every hypothesis of the cited nodes (the depth formula needs flatness, Hartogs needs finite stalks of depth ≥2, the fpqc cover is [d] of finite presentation). The new nodes are all true and none is a duplicate. Vertical-Cartier: smooth over normal gives G normal integral, the prime divisors off G_U are p^{-1}(Z), and the orders compare at the DVR of each Z. Big-open: extend at each DVR point, spread out, glue by full faithfulness. Power-prolongation: the symmetry hypothesis is needed (the cone-over-E Poincaré counterexample rules out the non-symmetric case); it holds with d=2 via Δ*Λ(N)≅N² and biextension extension (MB II 3.6 / Lan 3.3.2.6), and it is strictly smaller than the item, whose real work is removing the power. Multiplication-square: MB I 5.5 over any base. Multiplication-fppf: fibrewise isogeny plus the fibrewise flatness criterion. None of them duplicates lem-sfb-smooth-integral-fibre-vertical-divisors, lem-sfb-regular-group-rigidified-line-extension, lem-sc-mult-n-pullback, lem-sfb-semiabelian-invertible-multiplication or lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat. Edge cases checked: d=1, [p] on G_m in characteristic p (nonreduced kernel), U=S, a trait, non-ample lines. No SGA is cited. The off-unit tool_uses are generic and accepted. Advisory: whoever splits the power node later should use the biextension route and must not go through lem-sfb-symmetric-ample-power-extension, which now cites this item. No changes made.
